newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure as overseas markets and North American bonds weakened. * Analysts said risk is that TSE may follow New York's steep losses.
Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure on Monday as overseas markets and North American bonds weakened and gold bullion gave up some of its recent gains.
MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie said the risk is that Toronto may be unable to resist matching New York's steep losses after avoiding much of Friday's sell-offy.

"If we stay above 6700...the damage will obviously be limited. The problem is what is going on in the U.S. market if they continue to sell off, then the TSE will give back part of last week's 112-point gain," Beattie said.
Toronto stocks ended mixed on Friday, avoiding Wall Street's huge sell-off as Toronto's heavily weighted gold sector rocketed up on stronger bullion prices.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 16.94 points on Friday to close at 6738.19, snapping a string of six consecutive record sessions.
But Beattie said gold will not help Toronto at the open, as COMEX August gold slipped US$0.80 an ounce in early dealings to trade at US$328.80.
"So everything points to a negative start to the day," Beattie said.
In economic news, Canadian retail sales rose 0.5 percent in May to a seasonally adjusted C$19.25 billion from a revised C$19.16 billion (C$18.88 billion) in April.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.6 percent rise in retail sales in May after April's revised 1.2 percent (1.1 percent) increase.
